fix(render): a passage keeps only the effect it draws, and each depth of a bar is compared at one instant (candybar-joiners-e5r4.0hr)

High review pass on #496:
- Passage keeps the transition's done and its grounded effect, never the transition as made, whose own effect veils toward the terminal's ground.
- colour-256 draws every render of a comparison at one instant, so the depths compared are the same bar glyph for glyph.
- The audit, segment-render-unit and engine comments say what rich-js 0.25 does: one ground gets a lifted arrow; tween, loop and glyphs are refused as unknown functions.

fix(render): bump rich-js to 0.25 so every join is an arrow, and the tests say so (candybar-joiners-e5r4.0hr)

rich-js 0.25's joiner has no divider: it always draws its seam and lifts
an arrow's ink off a ground it would vanish into. The seam adapters
follow the new SeamForm (plainWith has no divider; the glyph probe draws
two cells), the glyph lists and doctor fixtures lose U+E0B1, and the
docs' render fences and the two byte snapshots show U+E0B0 where U+E0B1
was, each a lifted arrow between the door and its rate cell.

The reversed tests' arrow checks read the lift: in colour-256 an arrow's
ink is its cell's ground wherever that stands off the next ground as
drawn, and otherwise the colour rich-js's own joiner draws for the two
truecolor grounds, at truecolor, 256 and ansi. The theme-identity audit
reads an arrow's left side from the column before it, since the ink no
longer says it.

The 33 other rich-js commits in 0.25.0 change four APIs the render
uses: Effected takes its time from RenderOptions.frame, an effect frame
carries CellLook attributes, Transition is a class with a schedule, and
animationFuncs takes a TemplateFrame (only frames and stepped are
registered, as before).

test: any divider between two neighbouring cells fails (brandon-menus-sjhy.57p)

Brandon: "Take any tests that assert this state and reverse them, so any
occurance of this state makes the tests fail." The equal-bg test, the menu
seams' theme's-own allowance, the 256/ansi divider floor and the theme
identity audit's divider rule each accepted the divider; each now fails on it.

fix(plugins): a failed plugin's insert cell shows its drop, and a diagnostic's copy click names its message by key (candybar-plugins-vf6g.odm)

An insert cell placing a segment of an installed plugin that failed to load
now stands in and reaches the drop, so the drop shows in the ⚠ viewer
exactly as a tree placement of it does, instead of only in the daemon log.
An insert cell anchored on a cell of a plugin absent from the session is
absent with it: not placed and not reported as a missing anchor.

A diagnostic's copy click (its first line and ⧉ alike) now carries only the
message's key. The copy-diagnostic verb reads what to copy from the
session's last draw, so frame bytes no longer grow with the fix prompt and
terminals that cap OSC 8 link length keep the click. A key the last draw no
longer lists is refused loudly through the click error.

Placement presence is passed to the cross-reference walk as a parameter
rather than through the shared validation context, and one reportable
predicate decides which placements are errors at every site.
feat(plugins): a missing segment is an error only when its plugin is present, and its error copies a fix prompt (candybar-plugins-vf6g.odm)

fix(var-system): a watch_file path is heard wherever its link chain can change, by the rule the config watcher shares (brandon-unfiled-3248.sy24) (#495)

* fix(var-system): a watch_file path is heard wherever its link chain can change, by the rule the config watcher shares (brandon-unfiled-3248.sy24)

A `watch_file` source followed its symlink to the final target and watched
only that target's directory, so re-pointing a link (`ln -sfn`) or a dangling
link's target appearing refreshed nothing.

The config watcher's target builder moves whole into the watcher registry's
module as the one rule for where a set of paths can change: every hop of each
path's link chain, by name in its nearest existing directory, names unioned per
directory, a directory watched whole overriding them. The config watcher and
the var-system watch both call it.

A link walk the kernel stops (a loop, a readlink racing a delete) now keeps
the hops it reached instead of falling back to the spelled path, so a link
re-pointed by delete-then-create is still heard where it reappears. The writer
keeps its throwing view of the same walk.

The var-system watch holds each directory as open or failed, reconciled to the
set at every re-derive, so an unchanged directory is never reopened and a
refusal touches only its own directory. Its fault is derived (walk stops plus
failed directories), reported to every subscriber including late ones, and
clears when the cause does. A handle error, which previously had no listener
and would have taken the daemon down, now fails its directory, re-reads every
subscriber, and reopens at the next event-driven re-derive.

`isDirectory` goes; plugin-install asks `canonicalDirectory`, the one answer
to "is this an existing directory".

* fix(var-system): a watch_file directory recreated at its path is watched again, and a link gone before its readlink ends the chain (brandon-unfiled-3248.sy24)

Linux's inotify follows the inode, so a handle on a directory removed and
made again at its path heard nothing more and said nothing. Each open
handle now carries the folder identity it bound, and a re-derive reopens
any whose directory has moved.

A link removed between its lstat and its readlink is the chain ending,
the same fact as a link already gone, not a stopped walk: a non-atomic
`ln -sf` no longer flashes a watch fault.

* fix(daemon): the shared watch rule spells the folders a watch binds, so a config directory made again at its path rebinds (brandon-unfiled-3248.sy24)

The config watcher's key named only its target set, so on Linux a config
directory removed and made again at its path (a dotfiles re-stow) kept a
handle on the deleted inode and heard no edit after. The rule every file
watcher shares now reads each directory's folder identity once and spells
it into the watch's key; the config watcher keys on it, and the
watch_file manager compares against it instead of reading its own.

* fix(daemon): a watch keeps what it holds while a directory binds nothing, and a name-filtered watch hears its directory's own removal (brandon-unfiled-3248.sy24)

Folding folder identity into the config watcher's key left two holes. A
derive racing a directory's replacement read it as gone, changed the key,
and traded a working watch for a slot the OS refused; the registry's
`follow` now keeps a held watch while any directory of the spec binds
nothing, the rule git applied on its own, which moves into `follow`.
And the registry's name filter dropped Linux's report of a watched
directory's own removal (a rename under its own name), so the config
watcher never derived again to rebind; that event now passes. macOS
reports a change under the directory's name whenever a child comes or
goes, and its watch follows the path, so a change does not.

The watch_file manager keeps a held handle the same way, and builds its
entry from a derive rather than a placeholder.

* docs(memory): why a file watch's key names each directory's identity, and which self event a name filter lets through (brandon-unfiled-3248.sy24)

## [1.165.0](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/compare/v1.164.1...v1.165.0) (2026-10-30)

### Features

* **plugins:** a repo's own plugins load as repo.<name> beside installed plugins.<name> (candybar-plugins-vf6g.3gg) ([#489](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/issues/489)) ([c7c3ecd](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commit/c7c3ecda46896168f06ef5bc176b5bb541bd0a28))

### Bug Fixes

* **daemon:** the update act is a job every daemon reads, so it finishes whatever happens to the daemon that started it (brandon-unfiled-3248.z676) ([#491](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/issues/491)) ([3ac1f0e](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commit/3ac1f0ebd17dcc49615d30cb2f79602aa362240d))
test(colour): drop the DecorEntry import the deleted row-ground test left unread (candybar-joiners-e5r4.dg6)

docs(colour): the colour design doc states the open menu's named shades, not the search they replaced (candybar-joiners-e5r4.dg6)

COLOUR-FROM-THEME-VOCABULARY.md is ACTIVE and is where the colour memory
sends a reader for the rationale, but its rule, region table and
disclosure rules still described the state search, the plane's
recession and the floors as current. They now state the selected
shades; a dg6 entry in Decisions says what it supersedes and points to
PROPOSAL-joiners.md for why, and "What was deleted" lists the symbols.
test(colour): the palette-identity walk names its one exemption, and why authored backgrounds need none (candybar-joiners-e5r4.dg6)

fix(colour): the activated segment and its menu plane wear named theme shades; the inter-cell floors go (candybar-joiners-e5r4.dg6)

The segment whose menu is open, the ✕ and blank leads of that menu's rows,
and the plane the rows sit on now select colours the theme names, the way
every closed cell already does. The activated state is the menu hue at a new
`activated` column of the shade table: the hue's muted form on every window
of the ladder, its second lightening on the `muted` position. The plane is
`surface` at every depth. Items are unchanged.

Deleted: the open-trigger colour search and its rays, the plane blend and
its floors, the band item repair at 256 and ansi, every floor stated in
STATE_FLOOR, BAND_FLOORS or SEAM_MIN_DELTA_E, the shortfalls a band carried,
and the `band-floor` render warning with its cases in check and the daemon.
A disclosure no longer carries the ground its row dealt, since nothing reads
it. Text is unchanged: it is still chosen to clear AA on whatever it is
drawn on.
